the_prediction: r76, before running: if sequencing is the constraint, a per-step causal gate plus a retry should recover a meaningful part of the 37 parsed-but-failed tasks.
verdict_on_the_prediction: WRONG for the gate, RIGHT for sequencing. The first gated run with two bugs scored 14/130 -- worse than having no gate. After fixing submit-gating and typing it scored 18/130. The gate alone is not the mechanism.

what_the_gate_actually_did.honest_reading: the gate did its job -- it noticed steps that changed nothing. That did not win tasks by itself. Acting more than once, on a named target per step, is what won tasks.

the_flaky_result_and_why_it_is_recorded.what_happened: click-menu scored -1 -> 0.898 in the buggy run and -1 again in the final run, two runs apart, same code path
the_flaky_result_and_why_it_is_recorded.consequence: a single run per task cannot separate 18 from 14. The 18 is not a stable measurement and must not be quoted as one.
the_flaky_result_and_why_it_is_recorded.what_would_fix_it: N seeds per task and a pass^k style statistic, which is exactly the criticism levelled at tau2 and at every single-seed agent benchmark

the_fifteen_wrong_clicks.why_it_matters: these are not failures of inaction. The system clicked the wrong thing and was punished for it. A refusal would have scored 0; the agent scored below zero. That is worse than doing nothing, and it is the direct cost of acting without understanding the widget.

what_this_does_not_prove: that any change beat published systems
